entries.behavior: An RPC bind host already expressed as a bare IPv4 address passes through unchanged and can start the RPC server.
A configured IPv4 host with a data-plane port is stripped to the bare host before RPC server binding, allowing the server to start.
Decimal and 0x/0X hexadecimal object keys parse as complete unsigned sequence hashes, while empty, malformed, and trailing-garbage keys are rejected.
A disabled KV-event publisher is a no-op for stored and removed notifications and leaves published and dropped counters at zero.
When the KV-event queue reaches capacity, the publisher drops the oldest event, retains newer events, and increments its dropped-event accounting.
Publishing an SGLang object key over ZMQ emits a three-frame message with sequence, stored event type, backend, tenant, group, object key, empty sequence hashes, and successful publish statistics.
Pinned-memory registration rejects duplicate and overlapping ranges while accepting an adjacent range, and each accepted range unregisters exactly once when released.
Pinned-memory quota rejects capacity beyond the configured limit, releasing a region refunds capacity, and a later full-size registration succeeds and unregisters once.
A failed native pin operation refunds its reservation so retrying the same range after native recovery succeeds and later unregisters exactly once.
A failed native unregister retains the address and quota reservation, preventing overlapping or capacity-consuming replacement registrations from reusing unsafe memory.
Copying host bytes to an accelerator pointer selects the matching device, switches to its device ordinal, performs a host-to-device copy, and preserves the bytes.
entries.reason: Rust FFI exposes copy_from_host but has no discoverable fake-device test for device selection, context switching, copy direction, and byte preservation.

entries.behavior: Copying from an accelerator pointer to host selects the matching device, switches to its device ordinal, performs a device-to-host copy, and preserves the bytes.
entries.reason: Rust FFI exposes copy_to_host but has no discoverable fake-device test for device selection, context switching, copy direction, and byte preservation.

entries.behavior: Pointer classification returns the accelerator device whose query reports device memory and preserves the reported device ordinal.
entries.reason: Rust tests raw pointer-kind enum decoding but not runtime device selection or preservation of a matching device ordinal.

entries.behavior: A null pointer is rejected before querying any accelerator device.
entries.reason: Rust classify_pointer delegates directly to native code and has no discoverable test proving null is rejected without a native device query.

entries.behavior: Adding and removing keys from the LRU policy updates its visible candidate count.
entries.reason: C++ stores an internal mutable LRU key queue, while Rust derives each eviction candidate set directly from the authoritative object catalog and has no separate add/remove lifecycle or candidate-count API. Rust victim ordering and catalog deletion behavior are covered at their product boundaries.

entries.behavior: LRU eviction returns the least recently used key first and moves updated keys behind untouched newer candidates.
The C++ FIFO policy keeps randomly removed keys in its internal lazy queue and reports the unchanged queue size until eviction cleanup.
entries.reason: C++ tests a lazy-queue implementation detail. Rust couples FIFO entries to its storage index and removes deleted records eagerly; externally visible deletion and eviction correctness are covered separately.

entries.behavior: FIFO eviction returns the oldest inserted key and key updates do not reorder later FIFO victims.

entries.behavior: An RPC deadline failure has a dedicated timeout error class, distinct from generic service failure, with a human-readable timeout message.
A configured short RPC timeout bounds an unanswered readiness call and reports timeout rather than generic RPC failure.
Republishing byte-identical RPC metadata is idempotent and leaves the original metadata available.
Republishing changed RPC metadata for an existing location is rejected and does not overwrite the original value.
Starting the HTTP metadata listener on an occupied address reports bind failure.

entries.behavior: Snapshot-only standby startup restores configured snapshot metadata, discards stale state, and exposes the restored sequence as applied progress.
Snapshot-only standby startup with no available snapshot succeeds from an empty metadata and sequence baseline.
If standby startup fails due to invalid snapshot configuration, promotion returns the same failure instead of hiding it.
An empty tenant identifier normalizes to the canonical default tenant while named tenants retain their value and default classification.
Canonical tenant validation accepts default and ordinary names while rejecting the reserved underscore prefix and control bytes.
Tenant identifiers provide stable lexical ordering and hash-key equality.
A scoped key preserves colons and path characters and round-trips by splitting only at the tenant/local-key NUL delimiter.
Scoped-key parsing preserves embedded NUL bytes in the local key after the first tenant delimiter.
A legacy key without a tenant delimiter parses as belonging to the default tenant without changing the local key.
A Unix-domain IPC connection transfers an exact raw request and response payload in both directions.
Unix-domain IPC transfers an SCM_RIGHTS file descriptor from the initiating endpoint and the receiver can use the same underlying file.
Receiving an SCM_RIGHTS descriptor with a shorter-than-required payload fails and closes the received descriptor.
Unix-domain IPC transfers an SCM_RIGHTS file descriptor from the accepting endpoint and the initiator can use the same underlying file.
Stopping the C++ background UDS acceptor wakes its accept loop and removes the listening endpoint.
entries.reason: Rust Dummy IPC exposes a caller-owned one-shot listener rather than the C++ background UdsAcceptor, so this internal accept-loop lifecycle is not a Rust API contract.

entries.behavior: Stopping the C++ background UDS acceptor shuts down active connections so blocked handlers wake and exit.
entries.reason: Rust Dummy IPC does not own a background acceptor or handler threads; connection and thread cancellation remain with its caller.

entries.behavior: A Unix-domain connector rejects a non-positive connection timeout before attempting to connect.
Connecting to a missing Unix-domain endpoint with a short timeout fails promptly and identifies the endpoint.
After a timed Unix-domain connect succeeds, the connector clears its temporary socket send timeout.
entries.reason: Rust UnixStream::connect does not install a temporary SO_SNDTIMEO, so clearing that C++ implementation detail is not applicable.

entries.behavior: Starting the C++ background UDS acceptor without a registered handler fails with an explicit handler error.
entries.reason: Rust Dummy IPC exposes no handler-registration or background acceptor API; callers invoke the one-shot listener and process the returned channel directly.

entries.behavior: Zstd compression and decompression round-trip a textual snapshot payload exactly.
Zstd compression and decompression preserve a binary byte-vector payload.
The C++ raw-pointer Zstd overload round-trips a caller-provided pointer and length.
entries.reason: Rust Zstd APIs consume safe byte slices/readers rather than exposing the C++ raw-pointer overload; byte preservation is covered at the safe API boundary.

entries.behavior: The C++ explicit-output-size Zstd overload reconstructs a payload when the caller supplies its exact decompressed size.
entries.reason: Rust streaming decompression discovers the output length and has no caller-supplied exact-size overload; exact byte roundtrip is covered separately.
